title: Skip MultiMesh buffer readback on mesh change when a custom AABB is set
body:
`MeshStorage::_multimesh_set_mesh()` (RenderingDevice) recalculates the AABB when the mesh changes and no CPU data cache exists. To do that it calls `RD::buffer_get_data()` on the instance buffer, which is a synchronous GPU readback, and then calls `_multimesh_re_create_aabb()`. The first thing `_multimesh_re_create_aabb()` does is return when `custom_aabb` is set, so with a custom AABB the readback result is never used.

This change checks `custom_aabb` before reading the buffer back. The two other places that recalculate the AABB already work this way: `_multimesh_set_buffer()` and the dirty-region update in `_update_dirty_multimeshes()` both check `custom_aabb == AABB()` before recalculating.

## When this happens

The stall happens on every mesh change when a MultiMesh has all of these:

- a `custom_aabb`
- instance data uploaded with `set_buffer()` (no per-instance setters, so no CPU data cache)
- a mesh that is swapped at runtime, for example for mesh-based LOD

Setting a custom AABB and uploading in bulk is the recommended fast path. Vegetation that swaps meshes for LOD hits this stall on every LOD transition. In one of our grass scenes, the readback fences added up to about 9–16 ms per frame.

## What does not change

- MultiMeshes without a custom AABB still recalculate their bounds exactly as before.
- The CPU data cache path is unchanged.
- The indirect command buffer update, the same-mesh and zero-instance early returns, and `DEPENDENCY_CHANGED_MESH` still run.
- `_multimesh_get_aabb()` already returns `custom_aabb` when it is set, so culling sees the same bounds.

## Testing

This branch has not been built or tested yet. The same one-line change is applied in a downstream 4.7.2 fork, which has not been built there either. I will add test results here once I have them.
